key_agent_trends: EU Horizon Europe opens €297 million for frontier AI, robotics and energy-efficient infrastructure to advance technological sovereignty.
European open models emerge with OVHcloud's Olala Mini, a frugal 7B MoE LLM trained on public EuroHPC supercomputers.
Agent platforms deploy on sovereign cloud: H Company makes computer-use agents available on AWS European Sovereign Cloud for EU data residency.
Personal sovereign AI advances with Munich's RHISE AI raising angel funding for GDPR-compliant Lucie assistant.
Always-on and computer-use agents continue expanding in consumer and enterprise tiers globally.

stories.headline: OpenAI tests always-on Dots agents with select ChatGPT Plus users, expands to Business Standard
stories.what_happened: OpenAI began testing its always-on Dots agents with a small number of ChatGPT Plus subscribers outside the EEA, UK, and Switzerland. The company is also rolling Dots out to eligible US Business Standard members. Each Dot runs on its own cloud computer, works in the background toward goals, connects to thousands of apps via plugins, and is powered by models such as GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Terra. Official help documentation confirms the gradual rollout.
stories.why_it_matters: Extending always-on agents from high-tier plans to the popular $20 Plus tier accelerates mainstream adoption of proactive, persistent agents and intensifies competition with similar offerings from Google and Microsoft.

stories.headline: Anthropic opens Claude computer use beta to Team and Enterprise plans with admin controls
stories.what_happened: On November 20, Anthropic added computer use (beta) to Claude Team and Enterprise plans. The feature lets Claude see a user's screen and operate permitted desktop apps in the new unified Claude experience. It is off by default; only Owners can enable it, with role restrictions on Enterprise, app allow/block lists, and MDM controls. Rollout is gradual to organizations.
stories.why_it_matters: Bringing controlled computer-use agents to business plans enables enterprise adoption of desktop automation while addressing security and governance concerns through admin-only activation and granular restrictions.

stories.headline: Major US banks update terms to make customers liable for third-party AI agent actions in accounts
stories.what_happened: Wells Fargo, JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America, Citibank, and PNC have revised customer agreements or issued warnings regarding AI agents. Wells Fargo's updated Online Access Agreement, effective around November 24, states that use of any AI Agent is at the customer's own risk and holds users responsible for agent activities until revocation is notified. JPMorgan bans external agents logging in with credentials. Banks are building their own agents while restricting third-party access.
stories.why_it_matters: As AI agents gain the ability to act on financial accounts, banks are clarifying that customers bear the liability for mistakes, unauthorized actions, or prompt-injection risks, shaping the legal and practical boundaries of agentic finance.

stories.headline: Perplexity launches Monitor API to push scheduled web and page changes to AI agents via webhooks
stories.what_happened: Perplexity released the Monitor API, which runs scheduled web searches or page checks and delivers only relevant changes to applications or AI agents through webhooks. It supports Search monitors for topics and Page monitors for up to 10 specific URLs, with a judging model filtering for relevance and freshness. Pricing is $1 per 1,000 successful runs or fetched URLs. Available now via the Perplexity API.
stories.why_it_matters: It enables agents to stay continuously informed about changing information without constant polling, reducing token costs and improving responsiveness for research, monitoring, and proactive workflows.

stories.headline: European Commission opens €297 million Horizon Europe calls for AI, robotics and energy-efficient infrastructure
stories.what_happened: On 17 November 2026, the European Commission opened two Horizon Europe calls with 12 topics totaling €297 million under the Digital, Industry and Space work programme. €107 million targets frontier AI with safety by design, AI-enabled robotics, AI uptake in key sectors and solutions for low- and middle-income countries. €112 million supports energy-efficient AI processing, distributed computing and sustainable AI data centres. Proposals are due by 18 March 2027.
stories.why_it_matters: The funding advances EU technological sovereignty by supporting European AI development, robotics and infrastructure while reducing external dependencies.

stories.headline: OVHcloud announces Olala Mini, an open-source 7B European LLM trained on public supercomputers
stories.what_happened: On 17 November 2026, OVHcloud announced Olala Mini 7A1B, a mixture-of-experts model with 7 billion total parameters and 1 billion active, using hybrid attention. It runs on 8 GB GPUs or CPUs, is licensed Apache 2.0, and was trained on EuroHPC systems Jupiter, MeluXina and Jean Zay. Qwant has adopted it for flash answers with reported speed and cost gains. Official launch at OVHcloud AI Summit on 19 November.
stories.why_it_matters: Demonstrates European capability to train and open-source efficient LLMs using public infrastructure, supporting sovereign AI and local deployment.

stories.headline: H Company deploys AI agents on AWS European Sovereign Cloud for EU data residency
stories.what_happened: On 16 November 2026, Paris-based H Company announced its agentic AI platform is available on the AWS European Sovereign Cloud. Inference for requesting European customers runs on NVIDIA instances within the EU, keeping customer content and metadata in the Union, while model training remains on global AWS infrastructure. A first financial services customer is using it.
stories.why_it_matters: Enables European organizations in regulated sectors to use advanced computer-use agents while meeting data sovereignty and resilience requirements.

stories.headline: Munich-based RHISE AI raises €2.66 million angel round for sovereign personal AI assistant Lucie
stories.what_happened: RHISE AI announced a €2.66 million angel round backed by over 40 investors including Andy Bechtolsheim, Prince Max von und zu Liechtenstein and others. The company builds Lucie, a privacy-focused personal AI that integrates user data under GDPR on European infrastructure. The app is available on iPhone and Mac in English and German.
stories.why_it_matters: Advances European sovereign personal AI alternatives amid restrictions on some US agent features in the EU.
